analysis.title: Asia Open - Oil plunges, equities focus on funding
key_insights: WTI and Brent fell about 8% to $96 and $104 on renewed US-Iran diplomacy hopes, after reports that Khamenei approved negotiations and President Trump said he prefers diplomacy over resuming military activity.
Equities largely ignored the oil drop and stayed focused on financing concerns, stretched AI-related capex expectations and a crowded macro calendar.
The NDX fell 1.39% to 1.4% and is about 10% below October's all-time high, which puts it in correction territory. Tech underperformed cyclicals and consumer discretionary names.
Spot VIX traded above 21 and skew remains highly elevated, showing heavy demand for downside protection ahead of the midterms and other key events this week.

Citi's equity trading strategy desk closed its positive views on hyperscalers and growth. It remains long strong vs. weak balance sheet stocks and sees Health Care AI (CGUSHCAI) as the best option for growth.
Long-dated USTs bull flattened. The 10y and 30y yields reached their lowest levels since September before paring gains.
Key rates catalysts this week are the US midterms on Tuesday, the quarterly refunding announcement on Wednesday (issuance guidance expected to get a major overhaul), and non-farm payrolls on Friday.
The dollar was broadly stronger across G10, with NOK and AUD the laggards and CHF and GBP strong. Citi sees risk skewed toward USD selling ahead of the midterms.
Gold rebounded 2%, recovering part of Friday's near 4% slump. US natural gas reversed earlier gains and fell with oil.
Apple reported a slight beat: EPS $2.10 on revenue of $114.48bn vs. consensus $2.00 on $113.47bn.

market_movers.rationale: Apple reported EPS of $2.10 on revenue of $114.48bn, against consensus of $2.00 on $113.47bn. The report calls it a slight beat.

sector_views.rationale: Tech bore the brunt of the selling and underperformed cyclicals. The equity trading strategy desk closed its positive views on hyperscalers and growth.
The equity trading strategy desk sees Health Care AI (CGUSHCAI) as the best option for growth.

earnings_insights: Apple reported EPS $2.10 on revenue $114.48bn, vs. consensus EPS $2.00 on revenue $113.47bn (reported, a slight beat).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Oil fell on renewed US-Iran diplomacy hopes, which eases energy price pressure.
Brent fell alongside WTI on the same diplomacy headlines.

The reading is firmly in expansionary territory. Citi economists would watch for signs that activity slows into 2027, and the survey anecdotes were mixed, citing elevated costs and uncertainty but continued strength in AI-related activity.
The report is due Friday and is a key rates catalyst this week.
Citi expects headline inflation to stay broadly steady.
Core inflation could edge down. Tourism-related services and durable goods prices should offset lower agricultural prices.
Citi is in line with consensus. A hike is fully priced, so the bar for a hawkish surprise is high, though the press conference should keep a hawkish tone.
New RBA forecasts should show higher inflation, which keeps upside risks to the cash rate.
Wage growth should stay sticky and unemployment should reach the top of the RBA's NAIRU band.
Stable monthly inflation supports the SNB staying on hold, as it has signalled little urgency to adjust rates.
Food and housing inflation should lose pace, broadly offset by a pick-up in transport.
Supports GBP strength ahead of the decision.

risk_factors: Financing concerns and stretched AI-related capex expectations are weighing on tech.
A crowded macro calendar this week: US midterms, the quarterly refunding, the BoE decision, the RBA decision and payrolls.
Heavy demand for downside protection, with elevated skew and VIX above 21.
The US-Iran diplomacy path could reverse, which would affect oil.
Mixed ISM anecdotes citing elevated costs and uncertainty, and possible slowing in manufacturing activity into 2027.
vol_and_positioning: Spot VIX traded above 21, nearly revisiting Friday's highs, and skew remains highly elevated, with heavy demand for downside protection ahead of key events this week.
Midterms implied vol for Nov 4: SPX 0.91%, QQQ 1.63%, IWM 1.21%.
Cash desk flows skewed toward Info Tech, Healthcare, Comm Services and Energy, with outflows in Financials and Industrials.
Long USD positioning was reduced last week. Leveraged net USD flows peaked in mid-October and have been declining since, so risk looks skewed toward USD selling ahead of the midterms.

On the eTrading FX desk, volumes were below average except EURNOK and EURSEK, which were highly active on the move lower in oil. Net flows skewed toward JPY, leveraged accounts bought CNH, and outflows led in CHF, NZD and NOK.
geopolitical: Reports that Iranian Supreme Leader Khamenei gave the green light to negotiate, and President Trump said he prefers a path to diplomacy over a resumption of military activity, drove the oil selloff.
US midterm elections on Tuesday Nov 4 are a key event risk for markets this week.
